cues: Mercury's two chlorides are opposites in almost every way.
Calomel, mercury one chloride, is made by precipitation from mercurous nitrate, or by grinding mercuric chloride with mercury.
It is white, insoluble, tasteless and non poisonous.
Corrosive sublimate, mercury two chloride, is made from mercury and excess chlorine, or by heating mercuric sulphate with salt.
It is soluble, covalent, and a violent poison, as its name warns.
